name: derivation_thresholds
description: Version 3 (Story 2.5): version 2's nine parameters unchanged, plus the three the claim-path classification reads. Superseding is a new document, never an edit — v1 and v2 stay exactly what Stories 2.1 and 2.2 shipped, so an ordering or a banner produced under either is still explainable. The path parameters live in THIS document rather than one of their own because claim_path is a registered derivation (AD-10) and DerivationThresholds is the single argument every registered derivation is built from; injury_capture and intake_required_documents are separate for the opposite reason — they parameterise services/claims commands, not derivations. pathMinorSeverityMax is the ceiling below which a claim can be classified minor: it is a path question, not a risk question, so it is its own parameter and not a second reader of riskMedMin — the two answer 'is this claim first-aid-only?' and 'how does this claim's dot get coloured?', and one must be retunable without moving the other. pathMinorRecoveryWindows is the qualifying condition beside it: the recovery windows short enough to count as no lost time. An empty list switches Path A off from the document, which is a legitimate thing to want and the reason the set is data. pathFatalitySeverityMin is set at the top of severity_score's domain because the schema Story 1.2 seeded carries NO fatality indicator of any kind, and the strongest statement it can make about a fatal outcome is a maximum-severity, permanently disabling injury the worker never returned from — see services/derivations/path_classification.py, which argues at length why a lower cut-off here would misclassify the seven seeded amputation claims (several of whom returned to work fully recovered) as death-benefit files. Replacing this proxy with a real column is recorded as deferred work.
